title: Service incident follow-up
scenario: An engineering team reviews a fictional outage, separates observations from hypotheses, and assigns investigation and prevention work.
transcript:
[00:00] Soren: Thanks for making time. This is the follow-up for yesterday's notification delay. We are here to agree what we know and what to investigate, not to decide who is at fault. I have a timeline on screen, and I will read the key times aloud so the discussion is understandable without it.
[00:28] Imani: The queue started growing at nine twelve. Our first alert arrived at nine twenty, and normal processing resumed at nine forty-one. Those times are from the test service logs. We should call this a delay, because the records we checked eventually completed; we have not found evidence that messages were lost.
[00:56] Dev: The deployment finished at nine ten, two minutes before the queue started growing. That makes it a reasonable suspect, but it is not proof. A worker also restarted around the same time. I do not yet know whether the restart caused the delay or happened because the worker was already struggling.
[01:24] Ruth: Support received six reports of late notifications. Two people retried the action because they thought nothing had happened, and one saw a duplicate confirmation after retrying. I have written fictional reproductions of those sequences for this meeting so we can discuss the behaviour without sharing customer messages.
[01:50] Soren: Thank you. Let us distinguish the delay from the duplicate confirmation. The first is established in the queue measurements. The second is a reported sequence that we should reproduce. We should not claim that all delayed notifications were duplicated just because one retry behaved that way.
[02:16] Imani: The recovery step was to restart the stalled worker group. That reduced the queue, but it does not explain why the workers stalled. We have used the same recovery step before for a different problem, so a successful restart is not enough evidence to name this incident's root cause.
[02:43] Dev: I can compare the worker traces from before and after the deployment. My first thought is a connection pool limit, because the new code holds a connection slightly longer. I want that recorded as a hypothesis. I have not measured the pool during a reproduction yet.
[03:09] Ruth: For the support update, can we say the service is operating normally and that we are investigating the cause? I want to avoid telling people we fixed a specific defect when we have only restored processing. They will reasonably expect that distinction if the symptom returns.
[03:35] Soren: Yes. That is the update we can support. Ruth will send the service-status note through the normal support process today. Say that processing recovered and investigation continues. Do not promise that recurrence is impossible or identify the connection pool as the confirmed cause.
[03:59] Imani: On alerting, the queue exceeded our usual threshold several minutes before the alert arrived. The rule waits for a sustained increase to avoid waking someone for short spikes. I can simulate a shorter window, but changing it immediately could create alerts whenever a large scheduled batch starts.
[04:25] Dev: Could we add an oldest-message-age check rather than only lowering the queue-size threshold? A big queue can be healthy if it moves quickly. An old message waiting while new messages pass through would tell us something different, and that may be closer to what happened yesterday.
[04:51] Imani: That is worth testing. I can replay the incident measurements against both rules and compare the ordinary batch period too. I will bring the comparison Friday. I am not proposing to enable the new alert today; we need to see whether it catches delays without constant noise.
[05:17] Soren: Agreed. The decision is to evaluate the age-based rule, not deploy it. Imani owns the comparison by Friday. Dev owns the trace analysis. Dev, is Thursday afternoon realistic for an initial result, including a note if the connection-pool hypothesis turns out to be wrong?
[05:42] Dev: Thursday afternoon is realistic for the comparison, but perhaps not for a complete root cause. I will report what I tested, what the traces show, and what remains unexplained. If the connection limit looks relevant, I will add a controlled reproduction before recommending a configuration change.
[06:08] Ruth: For the retry issue, I can write the exact steps from the support reports today. Someone will need to check whether repeating the action is supposed to create a second confirmation. The current help text just says try again, which may be making the situation harder to understand.
[06:35] Dev: I will take the reproduction after the trace comparison. I cannot promise it will be complete Thursday as well. Could we give it a separate task without a deadline for now? Otherwise the notes may turn two different pieces of work into one commitment that I cannot keep.
[07:02] Soren: That is fine. Ruth provides the steps today; Dev owns reproducing the duplicate confirmation, with timing not yet set. We should mark that deadline as not stated. I will revisit its priority after the trace result rather than silently assuming it is part of Thursday's delivery.
[07:28] Imani: There is also a wording issue in the recovery checklist. It says clear the queue, but we restarted workers and let queued jobs complete. Clear could be read as deleting pending work. I would like to change that phrase even before the technical investigation is finished.
[07:54] Soren: Please do. Change it to restart the affected worker group and verify that pending jobs complete. Add the check for queue age returning to its ordinary range. That is a documentation correction we can agree now, and it does not depend on knowing the root cause.
[08:20] Ruth: I will remove the generic try-again suggestion from the draft status note, but not from the entire help centre without review. In the note, I can ask people to wait for confirmation and contact support if their result is unclear. Is that within today's decision?
[08:45] Soren: Yes, for this incident note. A broader help-centre change remains open. We should also avoid telling people to repeat actions that may have already completed. Your note can acknowledge uncertainty without making them responsible for diagnosing the queue themselves.
[09:07] Dev: My final list is trace comparison by Thursday afternoon, followed by the retry reproduction with no deadline set. The connection-pool limit remains a hypothesis. There is no rollback planned based on this discussion, and I have not proposed a change to the production configuration.
[09:32] Imani: I have the alert-rule comparison for Friday and the checklist wording update today. I will keep the existing alert active while testing alternatives. I will attach both ordinary and incident examples so the next review can compare false alarms as well as missed delays.
[09:57] Soren: That captures it. Processing recovered at nine forty-one; root cause remains unconfirmed. We agreed on investigation, clearer recovery wording, and a factual support update. We did not approve a new alert threshold or a configuration change. Thanks for separating those details. The review is finished.
